fixes.explanation: Goshen never comes up in this declaration, friend. Here's what the worshiper says: “So we called out to the LORD, the God of our fathers; and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, toil, and oppression.” They called, and the LORD heard their voice and saw what they were going through. That's the answer. Rest in Goshen isn't on the list, and I think a pillow in Goshen is a lot less comforting than being heard.

Haran, friend? That's a long walk backward, and the worshiper never takes it. He says the LORD brought them to “…this place…” and gave them “…this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.” The LORD is taking them forward, into the gift. I've been moved around a lot in my life, from a bin to a counter to a drawer, but nobody ever sent me back to the bin. Forward is the direction here.

Foreigner is right, and look who got an invitation. Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…the Levite, and the foreigner dwelling among you…” That's a person just living among them, and the text hands them a seat at the celebration. I know a little about being the new one in the room, and a seat at the table is a beautiful thing, friend.

Fasts? Friend, the basket just got set down and the worshiper has bowed. Nobody's skipping the party! Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.” Rejoicing is the word for this moment, and I'd say a growling stomach is a poor fit for it.
